description: Replace the random forest with an sklearn MLPRegressor (512,128 ReLU, alpha=1e-3, early stopping) on standardized Morgan count fingerprints, with predictions clipped to the training label range.
Replace the random forest with LightGBM using objective='l1' (median-targeted MAE fitting), 800 trees at learning rate 0.05, keeping the same Morgan fingerprint features.

Stack LightGBM (L1), random forest and Tanimoto-kernel SVR via 5-fold OOF predictions and a non-negative linear meta-learner (LinearRegression(positive=True)), with base models refit on the full training set for test predictions.

Replace the fixed 800-round LightGBM fit with an early-stopped version (seeded 10% internal validation, lr 0.03, up to 3000 rounds, patience 100 on L1), then refit on all training molecules with 1.1x the best iteration count.

The job exceeds the 600 s limit because each of the 15 fits runs six base_predict calls (five inner folds plus the final fit), each training a early-stopped LightGBM, a 150-tree random forest and an SVR; I cut that work by using 3 inner folds, a higher LightGBM learning rate with a lower iteration cap, and a 60-tree forest.

Adds nine hand-written SMARTS count features (acids, tetrazole, amines, quaternary N, phenol, amide, hydroxyl, nitro) appended to the Morgan bits for the tree models, while the Tanimoto SVR keeps using only the bit columns.

Append 2048-bit atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints after the existing Morgan bits and SMARTS counts, so the Tanimoto SVR still uses only the Morgan columns (:N_BITS) and the LightGBM and RF members see the extra long-range features.

Append the 167-bit MACCS keys to the Morgan bit block in featurize (placed right after the Morgan bits so the SVR's [:, :N_BITS] slice still selects only Morgan bits) so the LightGBM, RF and stacked models see coarse functional-group presence features.

Append the 167-bit MACCS keys to the Morgan bit block in featurize (placed right after the Morgan bits so the SVR's [:, :N_BITS] slice still selects only Morgan bits) so the LightGBM, RF and stacked models see coarse functional-group presence features.

Append the full RDKit CalcMolDescriptors set (cleaned of NaN/inf and clipped to training 1st/99th percentiles, cached per SMILES to limit runtime) to the feature matrix so the models see polarity and size descriptors such as MolLogP, TPSA and MolWt.

The job timed out because the random forest splits over about 6,000 features (max_features=0.3) in each of its 90 base fits; switching it to sqrt and subsampling LightGBM columns cuts the cost enough to finish within 600 s.

Abort: the proposed Tanimoto-kernel SVR (SVR kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1, on binary Morgan fingerprints) is already implemented in the current train.py as the third stack member, so re-adding it would duplicate existing code.
Swap the random forest stack member for a CatBoost regressor with MAE loss (1000 iterations, depth 6), and switch the Morgan block to count fingerprints per the spec.

The 600 s timeout came from fitting the three base models six times per fold (five inner out-of-fold passes plus one final pass) across 15 fits. I removed the inner stacking loop and used a plain average of the three base-model predictions, which cuts the fits per fold from six to one.
Fit the stack to the residual of a least-squares linear baseline a + b*Crippen MolLogP on the training set, then add the baseline back to the test predictions.

Aborted the proposed 0.5/0.5 average of RandomForest and LightGBM because the current stack already learns a positive-weight blend of those two members, and a fixed average would require dropping the SVR member or the linear logP baseline, which are the largest gains so far.
Change the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 (keeping 2048 bits) so the fingerprint captures larger substructures, with no other changes.

Make the Morgan block chirality-aware (includeChirality=True) and append a second count-based Morgan block that uses pharmacophoric feature atom invariants (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen), placed after the existing blocks so the first N_BITS columns that the Tanimoto SVR uses are unchanged.
Replace the Tanimoto-kernel SVR stack member with closed-form kernel ridge regression (Tanimoto kernel, lambda=0.5, training-mean centering), keeping runtime essentially unchanged.
Lower the LightGBM learning rate to 0.01 with 3000 rounds, and add bagging (fraction 0.8, freq 1) and min_child_samples=10 to the L1 LightGBM base model.

The job timed out because each of the 15 outer fits trains about 6 LightGBM models with 3000 trees and 6 random forests on roughly 6000 features, so I cut LightGBM to 600 trees at learning rate 0.05 and the forest to 100 trees.

Aborted the RF max_features/min_samples_leaf change: the spec's starting values (max_features=0.3, 300 trees) do not exist in the current file, and the literal 0.15 fraction on about 6,000 features would very likely exceed the 600 s job limit.
Adds a fourth stack member, a LightGBM (L1) model trained only on the clipped RDKit physchem descriptor columns, and widens the OOF matrix and meta-learner to four inputs.

issues: No integrity problems: no file or network access, no hardcoded answers, the test labels are not used, and the seed is passed to XGBRegressor.
Recomputed z = (0.5025-0.5087)/(0.0042*sqrt(2)) = -1.04, which matches the reported -1.045 up to rounding. The candidate is about 0.006 worse, consistent with reject.
Cosmetic: the variable name 'lg' now holds an XGBRegressor, which is misleading.

The learning rate is hardcoded to 0.03 instead of using LEARNING_RATE, and max_depth=6 and subsample=0.8 are added. Several changes are mixed into the model-family swap, so the comparison is not a clean ablation.

description: Replace the LightGBM (L1) stack member with an XGBoost regressor using reg:absoluteerror, 800 rounds, learning rate 0.03, depth 6, subsample 0.8 and colsample 0.3 on the full feature matrix, keeping the same number of boosting models; runtime near the 600 s limit is the main risk.
Switch the Morgan block in featurize from presence bits (GetFingerprintAsNumPy) to radius-2, 2048-bit count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), leaving everything else unchanged.

Replace the RandomForestRegressor stack member with a LightGBM regressor (num_leaves 31, 600 trees, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every round, min_child_samples 10) trained on the same feature matrix.

Replace the single-logP linear baseline with a least-squares fit of y on Crippen logP plus the six ionizable SMARTS counts (acid, tetrazole, sulfonic acid, acyl sulfonamide, basic amine, quaternary N), subtract that baseline before the stack, and add it back to the test predictions.

Append the 192-value CalcAUTOCORR2D topological autocorrelation vector to the cached RDKit descriptor vector (clipped and cleaned with the existing path); BCUT2D is already included in CalcMolDescriptors, so it is not added again.

The job timed out because each of the 15 fits ran a 5-fold nested out-of-fold stacking loop, so every fit trained the three base models about 6 times; I replaced the stacking with one training pass and an unweighted mean of the three base predictions, and removed the now-unused imports.

Regularize the L1 LightGBM member in base_predict with extra_trees, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=5.0, colsample_bynode=0.5 and subsample=0.8 (bagging every iteration), leaving the other settings unchanged.

Adds a fourth stack member, an SVR (precomputed kernel, C=5, epsilon=0.1) on a MinMax similarity over the atom-pair and torsion count blocks, computed once per fit via threshold decomposition with float32 matmuls so it stays fast.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement. The new knn_wmedian base learner uses only Xtr/ytr. In the inner out-of-fold loop it compares validation rows against training rows, so no row is matched to itself. At test time it uses only test features against training labels. No file access, no pasted values, no use of test labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. argpartition with k=10 needs more than 10 training rows, which always holds here. The weighted-median logic is correct: targets are sorted, cumulative weights are taken, and it picks the first position at or above half the total weight. The meta-learner's out-of-fold matrix grows from 3 to 4 columns, matching the new learner.

This is not a new problem with this diff: the inner stacking KFold is not grouped by scaffold. That makes the out-of-fold predictions optimistic, and a near-neighbour model like kNN gains the most from that, so the meta-learner may give it too much weight. That would hurt the outer score, not inflate it, so it is not a reason to veto.

Recomputed z: the candidate scored 0.4885 and the incumbent 0.4882, so the candidate is 0.0003 worse (lower is better). With sd 0.0042 per run and one run each, z = -0.0003/(0.0042*sqrt(2)) ≈ -0.05. The harness reports -0.045, which fits once you allow for the 4-decimal rounding. The change is pure noise and it adds code, so the reject decision is correct.

description: Add a fourth stack member, a Tanimoto kNN regressor (k=10, weighted median of neighbour targets with weights similarity^3) over the Morgan bit block, and widen the OOF matrix to four columns.

Add a fourth stack member, an RBF SVR (C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the standardised, 40-component PCA projection of the clipped RDKit descriptor block, and widen the OOF matrix and meta-learner to four columns.

Add Crippen logP and RDKit TPSA (standardised with training mean/std) as extra meta-learner inputs, entering as unconstrained linear terms via +z/-z column pairs under the positive-only LinearRegression.

Replace the least-squares positive-weight meta-learner with an L1 (MAE) meta-learner solved as a linear program via scipy linprog (HiGHS), keeping non-negative stack weights, a free intercept, and the logP baseline and final formula unchanged.
Append the RDKit ErG reduced-graph fingerprint (315 floats, NaN set to 0) as a new final block of the featurize feature matrix, leaving the existing blocks in their current order.
Append the RDKit ErG reduced-graph fingerprint (315 floats, NaN set to 0) as a new final block of the featurize feature matrix, leaving the existing blocks in their current order.
Weight each training molecule in the LightGBM fits by 1/(1 + number of other training molecules with Morgan Tanimoto similarity above 0.5), normalized to mean 1, so dense chemical series count less.

Run the inner 5-fold OOF stacking, meta-learner fit and full-data prediction under two inner KFold seeds (seed and seed+1000), average the two test predictions, and cut the LightGBM member to 400 rounds to stay under the 600 s limit.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and nothing hardcoded. The stacking OOF uses an inner KFold over the training rows only. The meta-learner is fit on train labels only. Test molecules are used only as features (Xte, Lte).

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The new `for s in (seed,)` loop runs once, so it matches the incumbent's single stack exactly. The averaging does nothing, and the inner KFold still gets random_state=seed. The only real change is N_ESTIMATORS going from 800 to 400.

Style: the one-pass loop and np.mean over a single prediction add code that does nothing. The card says to avoid this unless it is meant as a hook for multi-seed averaging. Base models still get `seed`, not `s`, so even with more seeds the base fits would not vary.

Recomputed z: using a difference sd of sqrt(2)*0.0042 ≈ 0.00594, z = (0.4882-0.4889)/0.00594 ≈ -0.118. The harness's -0.111 fits the unrounded values, since the 4-decimal rounding allows -0.10 to -0.135. The candidate is slightly worse and well within noise, so the decision to reject is consistent. Halving the trees may save runtime, but no timing was reported.

description: The job timed out because the nested stacking loop runs two full seeds, so each of the 15 outer fits trains the three base models about 12 times on ~6400 features; halving that to one seed brings the runtime under the 600 s limit.
Add a shrunken (x0.5) similarity-weighted nearest-neighbour correction, using the 5 most similar training molecules' OOF stack residuals on the Morgan block, on top of the final stacked prediction.
Early-stop the first LightGBM (L1) member on a seeded 15% Murcko-scaffold hold-out, then refit on all training rows with 1.1x the best round count, leaving the other two stack members unchanged.

The job timed out because each fit_predict ran base_predict six times (five inner stacking folds plus the final fit), each with an early-stopping probe LightGBM, so I removed the stacking loop and the probe and average the three base models' predictions in a single pass.
